citation.title: Rotational shear effects on edge harmonic oscillations in DIII-D quiescent H-mode discharges
citation.authors: Xi Chen, K.H. Burrell, N.M. Ferraro, T.H. Osborne, et al.

topic: Linear M3D-C1 and ELITE modeling of DIII-D QH-mode edge harmonic oscillations compared with magnetics, ECE, BES, ECE-I and MIR measurements; effects of E×B rotation scans.
own_question: Whether low-n EHO is a kink/peeling mode destabilized by edge E×B rotational shear.
actual_method_and_evidence: Offline analysis of DIII-D discharges 157102 and 153440. CER carbon profiles and E×B rotation were fitted and used as modeling inputs. Modeled mode structures were least-squares scaled to the fluctuation data. The rotation scan destabilized n=2 and stabilized n≥3. The authors note that the rotation and shear effects were not decoupled.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Pedestal carbon CER profiles (Ti, rotation, carbon density) are used offline as inputs to edge stability modeling, e.g. for E×B rotation estimation.
claim_checks.qualification: DIII-D only. Offline fitted profiles, not real-time. The text reports carbon impurity measurements, not main-ion Ti.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: CER at 200 Hz with ~0.6 cm pedestal resolution. BES and ECE at up to 500 kHz. Profiles were averaged over 25 ms windows. No nowcasting.
validation_if_relevant: Qualitative comparison of model with measurement. No held-out data and no predictive validation.
forbidden_inferences: Rotational shear mechanism shown for our data
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Different device, different question, and no estimation of temperature from fluctuation diagnostics. At most an optional background citation on offline carbon CER pedestal use.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
